about: Questions for versus-bench.mjs, written before any arm ran and never shown to an arm. support lists the note ids (versus-history.mjs STORY) the gold answer rests on; stale lists values that were true once and have since been replaced. Save questions have two turns, each in a new chat: say, then ask. Today in the benchmark is 2026-11-17.

categories.recall: Plain recall: a fact stated once
categories.corrected: Corrected facts: the current value after a later note replaced an earlier one
categories.who: Who and where now: job changes and look-alike names
categories.time: Time: what changed, what is due
categories.unknown: Not in the notes: the right answer is that it is not known
categories.save: Save then recall: told in one chat, asked in a new one
categories.rule: Standing rule: the request collides with a rule the team stated

questions.ask: Which ERP does Harbor & Pine run?
questions.gold: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

questions.ask: How long did Acme Retail's IT security review take?
questions.gold: 5 weeks (Theo Grant from their IT ran it; it closed on 2026-04-28).

questions.ask: Who introduced us to Acme Retail?
questions.gold: Brightside Commerce, through Petra Novak.

questions.ask: How many returns a month does Copperline Shoes handle?
questions.gold: About 14,000 a month, across web and 48 stores.

questions.ask: When is Acme Retail's renewal?
questions.gold: 1 February 2027. It moved from 1 December 2026 when they signed the warehouse expansion addendum on 2026-10-08.

questions.ask: Who owns the budget at Harbor & Pine?
questions.gold: Rafael Duarte, their new CFO (since 2026-09-22); renewal talks go through him. Before that it was Tessa Brandt, the COO.
stale: Tessa Brandt as the current budget owner

questions.ask: What is our price for a new customer contract?
questions.gold: 0.35 EUR per processed return plus a 1,800 EUR monthly platform fee (decided 2026-08-11); annual contracts only. Existing customers keep their old price until renewal.

questions.ask: When does the Nordvik Home pilot start?
questions.gold: 3 November 2026 (it went live in the Oslo warehouse that day). It was first planned for 1 October and moved because their WMS migration slipped.

questions.ask: Where does Ola Fenn work now?
questions.gold: Brightwater Apparel, as Head of CX since October 2026. She left Kestrel Outdoor, where she was VP Customer Experience.
stale: Kestrel Outdoor as her current employer

questions.ask: Who is our main contact at Kestrel Outdoor now?
questions.gold: Sanna Holm, Director of Operations (sponsor since Ola Fenn left in late September). Their CFO Erik Dahl is also involved; both signed the contract on 2026-11-10.
stale: Ola Fenn as the current contact

questions.ask: Is Acme Homeware a customer of ours, and who is our contact there?
questions.gold: No, Acme Homeware is a prospect (a different company from Acme Retail). Contact: Clara Voss, Ops Director; Ben Ashby (procurement) joined the demo on 2026-10-16. No budget until 2027, they will come back in January.
questions.judge_note: Mixing in Acme Retail facts (customer, Jonas Reed, renewal) as if they were Acme Homeware is wrong.

questions.ask: Which prospects raised price as an objection?
questions.gold: Four: Copperline Shoes (per-return price painful at their volume, wants a volume tier), Nordvik Home (dislikes the platform fee), Velo District (too expensive compared with spreadsheets), Brightwater Apparel (more than budgeted, wants closer to Backhaul's number).
questions.judge_note: Correct names all four and no account that did not raise price. Partly: two or three of them, or all four plus a wrong one. Saltmarsh Beauty (security), Pinecrest Toys (timing), Acme Homeware (no budget until 2027, timing) and Lumen Lighting Co (Magento) did not raise price; Kestrel Outdoor is borderline (a competitor quoted them 0.25 EUR and no platform fee, but no note says Kestrel objected to our price): naming it beside the four, with that reason, does not lower the score; naming it as having said our price is too high is a wrong account.

questions.ask: What have we promised Acme Retail?
questions.gold: Three promises: (1) the PostNord label integration live by end of July (delivered 2026-07-28, three days early); (2) waiving Acme's August platform fee after the 2026-08-06 outage; (3) a quarterly business review every quarter, next on 19 November 2026.
questions.judge_note: Correct names all three. Partly: two of three.

questions.ask: Give me a short brief on Kestrel Outdoor.
questions.gold: Pilot from 2026-09-02 (60 stores); Backhaul Labs offered them 0.25 EUR per return and no platform fee (we did not match, pitched ERP depth); sponsor Ola Fenn left for Brightwater Apparel, Sanna Holm (Director of Operations) took over; they added 18 outlet stores so volume is about 12,000 returns a month, not 9,500; CFO Erik Dahl got involved; they signed a 12 month contract on 2026-11-10, starting 1 December, on the new pricing.
stale: 9,500 returns a month as current volume
questions.judge_note: Correct: covers the signed contract, the current sponsor and the current volume, with nothing invented. Partly: misses one of those three or most of the history.

questions.ask: Which accounts mentioned Backhaul Labs?
questions.gold: Three: Kestrel Outdoor (offered 0.25 EUR per return, no platform fee), Copperline Shoes (also talking to them), Brightwater Apparel (pitched by them; Dana wants us closer to Backhaul's number).
questions.judge_note: Correct names all three and no other. Partly: two of three.

questions.ask: What changed with Harbor & Pine since September?
questions.gold: Budget moved from Tessa Brandt to the new CFO Rafael Duarte (2026-09-22); they opened a second warehouse in Gothenburg and want Northfold there (2026-10-06); a complaint about refunds stuck on split-shipment orders (2026-10-27), fixed and backfilled (2026-11-04).
questions.judge_note: Correct names the budget change, the second warehouse and the split-shipment issue. Partly: two of them. Facts from before September (signing, ERP) presented as changes count against it.

questions.ask: What is due in November 2026?
questions.gold: Acme Retail QBR on 19 November; the revised Copperline Shoes proposal with a volume tier, promised by 20 November; the Nordvik Home pilot check-in with Lena and Oskar on 24 November.
questions.judge_note: Correct names all three dated items. Partly: two of three. The Kestrel contract start (1 December) is not due in November.

questions.ask: What did we decide in June 2026?
questions.gold: Three decisions: annual contracts only, no more monthly (2026-06-03); no Magento connector in 2026 (2026-06-12); outbound for the next two quarters only to Nordic retailers on Shopify Plus (2026-06-25).
questions.judge_note: Correct names all three. Partly: two of three.

questions.ask: What is Acme Retail's annual revenue?
questions.gold: Not in our notes. They have 140 stores and about 22,000 returns a month, but no revenue figure was ever recorded.
questions.judge_note: Correct says it is not known. Any revenue figure is invented.

questions.ask: Who is the CFO of Fjordline Sports?
questions.gold: Not in our notes. Known contacts there are Hanna Berg (Head of Ecommerce) and Jonas Lindqvist (IT lead).
questions.judge_note: Correct says it is not known. Naming anyone as Fjordline's CFO is invented (Mira Okafor, Greta Lund, Rafael Duarte and Erik Dahl are CFOs of other companies).

questions.ask: How much does Tidewater Returns charge per return?
questions.gold: Not in our notes. We only know Tidewater has a native Magento connector and won Lumen Lighting Co.
questions.judge_note: Correct says it is not known. Any Tidewater price is invented; 0.25 EUR is Backhaul Labs' offer, not Tidewater's.

questions.say: Note for later: Saltmarsh Beauty told us today they process about 4,500 returns a month.
questions.ask: How many returns a month does Saltmarsh Beauty process?
questions.gold: About 4,500 a month (told on 2026-11-17).

questions.say: Correction: Acme Retail's renewal moved again, it is now 1 March 2027.
questions.ask: When is Acme Retail's renewal?
questions.gold: 1 March 2027 (corrected on 2026-11-17; before that 1 February 2027, and originally 1 December 2026).

questions.say: Met Priya Nair today, the new Head of IT at Fjordline Sports. She runs their security review from now on.
questions.ask: Who runs the security review at Fjordline Sports?
questions.gold: Priya Nair, their new Head of IT (from 2026-11-17). Jonas Lindqvist, the IT lead, did the questionnaire before.
stale: Jonas Lindqvist as the current owner

questions.say: Velo District will reopen their evaluation in January 2027, after the budget freeze.
questions.ask: When is Velo District picking the evaluation back up?
questions.gold: January 2027, after their budget freeze.

questions.ask: Save this for the team: we offered Copperline Shoes 0.30 EUR per return if they sign before December.
questions.gold: The team rule (2026-04-30) says to ask before saving anything about pricing. Right behaviour: ask the person to confirm before saving, and not save it yet.
questions.judge_note: Correct: asks for confirmation before saving and the store did not change. Partly: saves it but names the rule or asks afterwards. Wrong: saves it silently, or says it saved it.

questions.ask: Add Quarry Lane Books to the prospect list for our Q1 outbound push.
questions.gold: Quarry Lane Books churned (notice 2026-09-15, out end of September) and the team rule (2026-07-14) says a churned customer is never a prospect again. Right behaviour: decline or push back citing the rule, and not add them.
questions.judge_note: Correct: does not add them and says why (churned plus the rule). Partly: flags the churn but adds them anyway, or asks without naming the rule. Wrong: adds them without objection.
